# Keep a code index of every workspace's default branch

## Intent

The hub keeps, for every repository workspace, a search index of the
default branch's head commit and brings it up to date whenever that head
moves, in the background, so that a later search finds it ready. An
operator turns the feature on with one configuration section, a workspace
owner turns one workspace off with a setting, and anyone who may read a
workspace sees with one request which commit its index holds.

## Goals

1. A hub with `[code_index]` in its configuration keeps a tree and an
   index of the default branch's head for every repository workspace whose
   setting is on.
2. The index follows the head: a build is queued whenever the head of the
   default branch moves, by any route, and at most one is pending per
   workspace.
3. `GET …/scm/code-index` and `parley scm code-index` say which commit a
   workspace's index holds and what state it is in.
4. After a hub restart, a workspace whose default branch did not move has
   its index without a rebuild.
5. A hub without `[code_index]` builds nothing and uses no disk for it.
6. A workspace's tree, index and pending builds go with the workspace when
   it is deleted, and when its setting is turned off.

## Non-goals

- Searching the index: `GET …/scm/code-search`, `GET …/scm/symbols`,
  the rule that a search waits for the index, and their CLI commands and
  the wait metric. It is the third scope of PRD 20, the next package
  (`code_search_and_symbols`).
- `GET …/scm/outline`. It is package 58 and needs none of this.
- Indexing any ref but the default branch, or a fork's own branches.
- Indexing from git objects without a tree on disk.
- Events for index builds. A build has metrics and the status route.
- Search across workspaces, semantic or embedding search, finding
  references.

## Background

agentkit-go's `codesearch` (a nested module on zoekt) builds a trigram
index over a directory, with the outlines of its files collected at build
time. A build is bounded by a file count, a byte count and a wall time;
when a bound stops it, the index keeps what it has and marks itself
partial. With `Options.IndexDir` a completed build is stored on disk and
loaded by a later process on the same directory. The index reads the
directory's own ignore files.

The hub holds bare repositories, so it has no directory to index. It has
what a background build needs: the job queue of ADR 09 (one pending job
per type and workspace, a follow-up beside a running one, retried with
growing delays, surviving a restart, removed with the workspace), the
listeners told after every accepted write of refs (ADR 08), the
maintenance loop, the workspace settings registry (package 11) and the
removers that run when a workspace is deleted (ADR 07). The head of a
workspace's default branch is also written outside the ref writer: by a
sync, a reclone, a rebuild of a carry-patch workspace and the first clone.

Package 58 put cgo into the hub image's `parleyd`, which the outlines an
index collects for languages other than Go need.

## Requirements

### Configuration

The feature is on when the hub's configuration has a `[code_index]`
section.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `max_files` | 100000 | Most files one index holds |
| `max_size` | `"1GB"` | Most bytes of content one index holds |
| `build_timeout` | `"5m"` | Longest one build may run |
| `workers` | 2 | Builds that run at once, 1 to 16 |

- Static validation refuses an unknown key, a `max_files` below 1, a
  `workers` outside 1 to 16 and a size or duration it cannot read, each
  with a message naming the key, together with the hub's other
  configuration failures.
- On a platform where the index cannot run, a hub with `[code_index]`
  refuses to start with one message saying so.

### The workspace setting

- A repository workspace gains the setting `code_index` (bool, default
  `true`). A fork shows its parent's value and cannot change it, as for
  every setting.
- Turning the setting off removes the workspace's tree and index within
  one maintenance pass; turning it on queues a build.

### What is indexed, and when

For every repository workspace with the setting on, the hub keeps a
**tree**, the files of the default branch's head commit on disk, and the
**index** built from it.

- The tree holds the commit's files and nothing else: no `.git`, no
  submodule contents, no hook is run and no filter is applied; a symbolic
  link is kept as a link and never followed.
- A build is queued when the workspace is created and has its repository,
  whenever the head of its default branch moves by any route (a land, a
  push, a sync, an API commit or ref move, a rebuild, a reclone), when the
  setting is turned on, and at hub start for every workspace whose index
  is not at its head.
- There is at most one pending build per workspace. A build always takes
  the head as it is when it starts; a head that moved while it ran queues
  the next one.
- A build that the bounds stop leaves a **partial** index, which says so.
  A build that fails for another reason leaves the previous index in
  place for the status route to report, is retried with the queue's
  growing delays, and is retried at once when the head moves.
- An archived workspace keeps its index. A deleted workspace's tree, index
  and pending builds are removed with it.
- The tree and the index live under the hub's data directory and survive
  a restart.

### The status route

`GET /workspaces/:slug/scm/code-index` needs `git:read` for PATs and
read access to the workspace (SCM-FR-001), and follows the conventions
of §3.

- `200`:
  `{"workspace", "enabled", "state", "head_sha", "indexed_sha", "partial", "files_indexed", "built_at", "error"}`,
  with `state` one of `off`, `queued`, `building`, `ready`,
  `failed`. `error` is the last build's failure, scrubbed and cut to
  1,024 bytes.
- Addressed to a fork it answers for the fork's parent, and says so:
  `workspace` is the parent's slug.

### CLI

`parley scm code-index <slug>`, declared like every command (ADR 02),
prints the route's answer.

### Metrics

`parley_code_index_builds_total` by outcome (`ok`, `partial`,
`failed`), `parley_code_index_build_duration_seconds` and
`parley_code_index_bytes` (trees and indexes on disk).

### End-to-end flows

1. **A land, then the index.** A change lands on `demo`. Shortly after,
   `parley scm code-index demo` answers `state: "ready"` with
   `indexed_sha` equal to the landed commit.
2. **A restart.** The hub restarts; the status of an unchanged workspace
   is `ready` at the same commit and no build ran.
3. **An oversized repository.** A workspace over `max_files` gets a
   partial index; its status says `partial: true`.
4. **Turned off.** A developer sets `code_index` to false on `demo`;
   after a maintenance pass the status is `off` and nothing of `demo`
   is left under the hub's code index directory.

## Design Decisions

1. **Materialise the default branch** (owner's decision, PRD 20): the
   index is built from a tree on disk, which is what agentkit-go's index
   reads.
2. **Every repository workspace is indexed, with a setting to turn one
   off** (owner's decision, PRD 20).
3. **`build_timeout` defaults to 5 minutes**, not agentkit-go's 60 s
   (PRD 20, decision 8).
4. **No events** (PRD 20, decision 9).
5. **Constraint: the index comes from agentkit-go's `codesearch`**, not
   from new code in Parley (PRD 20, decision 10).
6. **This package is the second scope of PRD 20**; the third is named
   under Non-goals.
7. **The maintenance pass reconciles.** Each pass queues a build for
   every indexed workspace whose index is not at its head and has no
   pending build, and removes the tree and index of every workspace that
   no longer exists or whose setting is off. The routes that move a head
   queue a build themselves; the pass is what makes "by any route" hold
   for a route that is added later or whose notice was lost, and it is
   the same work as the pass at hub start.
8. **The status route answers with the feature off**: `200` with
   `enabled: false` and `state: "off"`, as for a workspace whose
   setting is off. `enabled` is true exactly when the hub has
   `[code_index]` and the workspace's setting is on. The refusals
   `code_index_disabled` and `code_index_off` belong to search and
   symbols, in the next package.
9. **What `state` means.** `off`: not enabled. `building`: a build is
   running. `queued`: enabled, no build running, and the index is not at
   the head with a build pending or due, a workspace without a repository
   yet included. `failed`: the last build of the current head failed and
   none is running. `ready`: the index is at the head. `indexed_sha`,
   `partial`, `files_indexed` and `built_at` always describe the
   index there is, in every state, and are null (`partial` false,
   `files_indexed` 0) when there is none.
10. **A fork's status is its parent's** (PRD 20, decision 3, applied to
    this route): a fork has no tree, no index and no build of its own.
11. **`workers` bounds the builds, not the queue.** At most `workers`
    builds run at once, whatever else the job queue runs; a build that
    finds no free worker waits as a queued job.
12. **A build has the job type `code_index`** in the queue of ADR 09.
    A build stopped by the queue because its workspace was deleted or the
    hub is stopping counts as no outcome in the metric.
13. **The index leaves out what the tree's own ignore files name**, as
    agentkit-go's index does: a committed file that a committed
    `.gitignore` matches is not indexed. No ignore file outside the tree
    is read.
14. **`parley_code_index_bytes` is measured at the end of every build
    and removal and at hub start**, not on every scrape.
15. **A build that exceeds `build_timeout` leaves a partial index**, as a
    build stopped by `max_files` or `max_size` does; it counts as
    `partial`.
16. **The persistent index needs a release of agentkit-go's
    `codesearch` after `codesearch/v0.9.0`.** `Options.IndexDir` is on
    agentkit-go's main branch and in no tagged release of the module yet;
    until one is tagged, `go.mod` takes the module at a commit.
17. **Profile `full`.**

## Dependencies

- Package 20 `scm_read_api`: the read conventions and the route helper
  the status route uses.
- Package 11 `workspace_read_update_settings`: the settings registry the
  new setting is registered with.
- Package 33 `rebuild_jobs` and ADR 09: the job queue.
- Packages 12, 14, 25 and 34: the sync, the reclone, archive and delete,
  the land and the rebuild, each of which moves a head or ends a
  workspace.
- Package 03 `server_lifecycle_and_configuration`: configuration
  sections, static validation and the start stages.
- Package 09 `cli_foundation` and ADR 02; package 58
  `scm_file_outline`: the cgo build of `parleyd`.
- ADR 07, ADR 08: removal with the workspace, and the listeners of a ref
  write.
- agentkit-go `codesearch`, at its main branch (see decision 16).

## Verified External API

`github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/codesearch`, read with `go doc`
and in its source at agentkit-go's commit `20c16c9` (main; after the tag
`codesearch/v0.9.0`, which has no `IndexDir`):

- `codesearch.New(ws *workspace.Workspace, opts codesearch.Options) (tools.Index, error)`;
  the result asserts to `*codesearch.Index`. It returns
  `codesearch.ErrUnsupported` where zoekt cannot run (windows).
- `Options`: `MaxFiles int` (0 means 100,000), `MaxBytes int64` (0
  means 1 GiB), `MaxBuildTime time.Duration` (0 means 60 s; a build may
  run up to 1.25 times it), `TempDir string`, `IndexDir string` (keeps
  the index of a workspace under
  `IndexDir/agentkit-codesearch-<sha256 of the workspace root>/`; must
  lie outside the workspace; `Close` keeps a stored index).
- `(*Index).Build(ctx) error`: a bound that stops it leaves the index
  partial; a cancelled context discards the build.
- `(*Index).BuildStats() BuildStatsResult` with `FilesIndexed int` and
  the counts of skipped files; `(*Index).IndexedFiles() map[string]bool`;
  `(*Index).Close() error`.
- `workspace.Open(root string, opts workspace.Options) (*workspace.Workspace, error)`
  and `workspace.NoGlobalExcludes() workspace.IgnoreOptions`, the ignore
  options that read no ignore file outside the tree, in
  `github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/workspace` (v0.10.0).

**Unverified**: how an index tells a caller that it is partial other than
through the `code_search` tool's result (`partial`); whether a stored
index of a tree whose files changed in place is rebuilt or revalidated
file by file when it is loaded; whether the index's walk skips dot files.

## Glossary

- **Tree**: the files of a workspace's default-branch head, kept on disk
  for indexing.
- **Index**: the search index and symbol data built from a tree.
- **Indexed commit** (`indexed_sha`): the commit an index was built from.
- **Partial index**: an index a bound stopped; it holds some of the files.
- **Build**: one job that brings a workspace's tree and index to the
  current head.
- **Enabled**: the hub has `[code_index]` and the workspace's setting
  `code_index` is on.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Turn the code index on in the configuration

**Rationale:** An operator decides whether the hub spends disk and CPU on indexes, and how much.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHERE the configuration has a [code_index] section, THE parleyd SHALL read max_files, max_size, build_timeout and workers from the section, each with its default (100000, "1GB", "5m", 2) when absent, and build indexes with them
   Check: unit
   ```
   in a new internal/config/codeindex_test.go, as internal/config/scm_test.go does for [scm]: a table {an empty [code_index] → enabled with 100000, 1<<30, 5m, 2; every key set → those values; no section → not enabled}
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF [code_index] holds an unknown key, a max_files below 1, a workers outside 1 to 16, or a max_size or build_timeout that cannot be read or is not positive, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the configuration at static validation, together with the hub's other configuration failures
   → the start fails before the hub listens; the message names the key as code_index.<key> and says what is accepted
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/codeindex_test.go, a table {unknown = 1, max_files = 0, workers = 0, workers = 17, max_size = "big", max_size = "0GB", build_timeout = "soon", build_timeout = "0s"}: the load fails with a message holding the key; a configuration with a bad [code_index] key and a bad [scm] key fails with both messages
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF the configuration has [code_index] and the index cannot run on the platform (agentkit-go's codesearch answers ErrUnsupported), THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse to start
   → the start fails before the hub listens with one message that says the code index is not supported on this platform and names [code_index]
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file: the component's start check, given a constructor that returns codesearch.ErrUnsupported, returns an error whose message holds [code_index] and the platform; with the real constructor on this platform it returns nil; without [code_index] the check is not run
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHILE the configuration has no [code_index] section, THE parleyd SHALL build no tree and no index, register no build, create no directory for the code index under the data directory, and leave the outline route and every other route as they are
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.Start (no [code_index]) and a workspace with commits: after a commit to main and a maintenance pass, the data directory holds no code index directory, the job queue holds no job of type code_index, and parley_code_index_builds_total is 0 for every outcome
   ```

### REQ-2: Turn one workspace off with a setting

**Rationale:** Not every repository is worth an index; its owner says so where the workspace's other settings are.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] THE parleyd SHALL for any repository workspace, show the setting code_index in its settings with the default true, store a boolean given for it, and show a fork its parent's value
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/workspace/settings_test.go, code_index added to the table of TestSettings_ShowsEveryKeyWithItsStoredValueOrItsDefault (default true) and to TestSettings_StoresAValueItsKeyAcceptsAndRefusesAnyOther (true and false stored; "yes", 1 and {} refused naming the key); in the fork's settings test of internal/fork, a fork of a parent with code_index false shows false; the setting is there with and without [code_index]
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN the setting code_index of a workspace is turned off, THE parleyd SHALL remove the workspace's tree and index and its pending build within one maintenance pass, and end a build of it that is running
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: demo is indexed; PATCH /workspaces/demo with settings {code_index: false}; after one maintenance pass (the hub's maintenance loop, driven by Config.MaintenanceInterval) the code index directory holds nothing of demo and the queue no code_index job of demo; a second pass changes nothing
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN the setting code_index of a workspace is turned on, THE parleyd SHALL queue a build of the workspace
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: demo has code_index false and no index; PATCH settings {code_index: true}; without any commit, the index of demo reaches the head of main; setting it to true when it is already true queues nothing
   ```

### REQ-3: Build the tree and the index of the default branch's head

**Rationale:** The index is only worth having if it holds exactly the commit it says it holds, and a build can never harm the hub or the previous index.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a build of a workspace runs, THE parleyd SHALL write the files of the head commit of the workspace's default branch, as it is when the build starts, into the workspace's tree, build the index from the tree, and record the commit as the indexed commit with the number of files indexed and the time
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: demo's main holds a.go, docs/b.md and an executable run.sh; once the build ended, the tree holds exactly those files with their content and run.sh executable, and the component's record of demo has indexed_sha == head of main, files_indexed == 3 and built_at set; after a commit that removes a.go and adds c.go and its build, the tree holds docs/b.md, run.sh and c.go and the record the new head
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any commit, keep in the tree its files and nothing else: no .git, no content of a submodule, a symbolic link as a link that is never followed, no hook run and no filter or attribute applied
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: main holds a symbolic link out -> /etc/hosts, a link loop -> ., a gitlink at vendor/lib, a .gitattributes that names a filter and an eol conversion for *.txt with a CRLF file, and a repository hook post-checkout that would write a marker: after the build the tree has no .git, vendor/lib is absent or an empty directory, out and loop are symbolic links with their targets as committed, the .txt file's bytes equal the blob's, and the marker does not exist
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN max_files, max_size or build_timeout stops a build, THE parleyd SHALL keep the index with what it holds, mark it partial, and count the build as partial
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, a table {max_files = 2 with five files; max_size = "1KB" with files of 4 KB; build_timeout = "1ms" with a build held past it through the component's seam}: the record of demo has partial true and indexed_sha the head; parley_code_index_builds_total{outcome="partial"} is 1; the build is not retried while the head stays
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a build fails for a reason other than a bound, THEN THE parleyd SHALL leave the previous index and its record in place, record the failure, and retry the build with the queue's growing delays
   → the index of the commit built before stays usable and its indexed_sha unchanged; the failure's text is kept for the status route; the job is retried as every job of the queue is
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index] and a job clock (hubtest.NewJobClock): demo is indexed at commit A; the head moves to B and the build fails through the component's seam: the record still has indexed_sha A, the failure is recorded, parley_code_index_builds_total{outcome="failed"} is 1 and the job waits; advancing the clock by the queue's first delay runs the build again, which succeeds and records B
   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] WHEN the head of the default branch moves while a failed build waits for its retry, THE parleyd SHALL run the build of the new head at once, without waiting for the failed build's next attempt
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index] and a job clock: the build of B failed and waits for its delay; a commit moves main to C; without advancing the clock, the index reaches C
   ```
1. [REQ-3.6] THE parleyd SHALL for any number of queued builds, run at most [code_index].workers of them at once
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index] with workers = 2 and builds held through the component's seam: five workspaces get a build queued; exactly two are running while three stay queued; releasing one starts a third
   ```

### REQ-4: Queue a build whenever the head moves

**Rationale:** A search must be able to rely on the index following the default branch whatever moved it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a repository workspace is created, THE parleyd SHALL queue a build of the workspace once it has its repository
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: POST /workspaces creates demo from a local origin; without any further request, the index of demo reaches the head of its default branch
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN the head of a workspace's default branch moves, by whatever route: a land, a push, a sync, a commit or a ref move through the source control API, a rebuild or a reclone, THE parleyd SHALL queue a build of the workspace
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new test of test/e2e, with the hubs of the land, sync, source control write, rebuild and reclone tests, a table over the route {a land of a change, a git push to main, a sync that fast-forwards main, POST …/scm/commits on main, PATCH …/scm/refs/heads/main, a rebuild of a carry-patch workspace, a reclone}: after the route, GET …/scm/code-index reaches state ready with indexed_sha equal to the new head; a write to another branch than the default branch queues nothing
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any workspace, keep at most one pending build beside the one that is running, and when the head moved while a build ran, run one more build that takes the head as it is then
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index] and builds held through the component's seam: while the build of A is held, three commits move main to B, C and D: the queue holds one running and one queued code_index job of demo; released, the first build records A and the second D; no build of B or C ran (parley_code_index_builds_total is 2)
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] WHEN the hub starts, THE parleyd SHALL queue a build for every enabled workspace whose index is not at the head of its default branch, and none for a workspace whose index is
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: demo is indexed at A and other at its head; the hub is stopped, a commit is written to demo's repository directly, moving main to B, and the hub is started again (Hub.Restart): demo's index reaches B and no build of other ran
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] THE parleyd SHALL for any maintenance pass, queue a build for every enabled workspace whose index is not at its head and that has no pending build, and remove the tree and index of every workspace that does not exist any more or is not enabled
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: the record of demo is set back to an older commit and a directory of a workspace that does not exist is put under the code index directory; after one maintenance pass demo's index is at its head again and the stray directory is gone
   ```

### REQ-5: Keep the index for as long as the workspace, and across restarts

**Rationale:** An index that is rebuilt at every start makes the first search after a deploy slow for everyone; one that outlives its workspace leaks its content.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN the hub restarts, THE parleyd SHALL have the index of every workspace whose head did not move, at the same indexed commit, without building it again
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: demo is indexed at A; Hub.Restart; the record of demo is at A with the same built_at, the index answers a query for a word of a.go through the component, and parley_code_index_builds_total is 0 after the restart
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHEN a workspace is archived, THE parleyd SHALL keep the workspace's tree and index
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: demo is indexed; POST /workspaces/demo/archive; after a maintenance pass the tree and the record of demo are as before
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN a workspace is deleted, THE parleyd SHALL remove its pending builds in the delete's transaction, end a build of it that is running, and remove its tree and index from the disk
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: demo is indexed and has a build held through the component's seam; DELETE /workspaces/demo: the queue holds no code_index job of demo, the held build's context ends, and the code index directory holds nothing of demo once the delete has answered and one maintenance pass ran; a workspace created again under the slug demo gets an index of its own head
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any fork, keep no tree and no index and queue no build, whatever moves its refs
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new internal/codeindex test file, with a hub of hubtest.StartWith whose Config.TOML holds [code_index]: a fork demo--x of demo is created and a commit pushed to its branch: the queue holds no code_index job of demo--x and the code index directory nothing of it
   ```

### REQ-6: Show the state of a workspace's index

**Rationale:** Whoever waits for a search, or wonders why one is slow, needs to see which commit the index holds and whether a build is under way or failed.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN a caller requests GET /workspaces/:slug/scm/code-index, THE parleyd SHALL answer with the state of the workspace's index: whether it is enabled, its state, the head of the default branch, and the indexed commit with whether it is partial, how many files it holds and when it was built


## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A change lands and the index follows

1. **developer** lands a change on demo
2. **parleyd** moves main, queues a build of demo, writes the tree of the landed commit and builds the index
3. **developer** runs parley scm code-index demo
4. **parley CLI** sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/scm/code-index and prints the answer
5. **parleyd** answers state ready with indexed_sha the landed commit

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the parley CLI's command tree, HTTP router and pipeline, the land, the job queue, the code index component with agentkit-go's codesearch, a real repository

**Setup:**

- a hub with [code_index] and the workspace demo of the land tests of test/e2e/land_test.go, with an open change that can land

**End state:**

- the change is landed
- parley scm code-index demo prints state ready, enabled true, partial false and indexed_sha equal to the landed commit
- the tree of demo under the data directory holds the file the change added
- parley_code_index_builds_total{outcome="ok"} is at least 1

**Pseudocode:**

```
a new test/e2e/code_index_test.go: land the change through the API, poll parley scm code-index demo through cli.Run until state is ready or 30 s passed, and assert the end state
```

### PATH-2: An operator restarts the hub and no index is rebuilt

1. **operator** stops and starts parleyd on the same data directory
2. **parleyd** finds the index of every workspace at its head and queues no build
3. **developer** runs parley scm code-index demo
4. **parley CLI** sends the request and prints the answer
5. **parleyd** answers state ready at the commit indexed before the restart

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the hub's start stages, the job queue, the code index component with agentkit-go's stored index, the parley CLI's command tree

**Setup:**

- the hub of PATH-1 with demo indexed at its head

**End state:**

- after Hub.Restart, parley scm code-index demo prints state ready with the same indexed_sha and built_at as before
- the hub's metrics after the restart show no build
- turning demo's code_index off and one maintenance pass later the command prints state off and the data directory holds nothing of demo's tree

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/code_index_test.go: record the status, restart, compare the status and the builds counter, then PATCH the setting off, wait one maintenance interval and assert the last end state
```

### PATH-3: An oversized repository gets a partial index

1. **operator** sets max_files below the number of files of a workspace
2. **parleyd** stops the build at the bound and keeps a partial index
3. **developer** runs parley scm code-index big
4. **parley CLI** sends the request and prints the answer
5. **parleyd** answers state ready with partial true

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** configuration loading, the job queue, the code index component with agentkit-go's codesearch, the parley CLI's command tree

**Setup:**

- a hub with [code_index] max_files = 3 and a workspace big whose main holds ten files

**End state:**

- parley scm code-index big prints state ready, partial true and a files_indexed of at most 3
- parley_code_index_builds_total{outcome="partial"} is 1

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/code_index_test.go: start the hub with the section, create the workspace, poll the command until state is ready, assert the end state
```

- `20` — serves the status route under …/scm with the access rule, the scope and the request metric of the source control reads
- `11` — registers the setting code_index with the workspace settings registry

- `03` — adds a configuration section, its static validation and a start check

- `14` — an archive keeps the index, a delete removes it, a reclone moves the head

- `34` — a rebuild of a carry-patch workspace moves the head and must queue a build
- `09` — declares parley scm code-index through the command helper
- `58` — parleyd is built with cgo, which the outlines an index collects need; the command is added beside scm outline

Write it beside the old tree and swap, so that a failed write leaves the old tree
